related_questions.question: What is the most unsurvivable cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Pancreatic cancer is often considered the deadliest and least survivable cancer due to its aggressive nature and often late stage diagnosis. While other cancers like lung cancer have higher mortality rates overall, pancreatic cancer's low five-year survival rate (around 8.3%) makes it particularly challenging to overcome.
Here's why pancreatic cancer is so difficult to treat:

list.title: Silent Symptoms:
list.snippet: Pancreatic cancer often has few noticeable symptoms in its early stages, leading to delayed diagnosis.

list.title: Aggressive Spread:
list.snippet: The cancer tends to spread quickly to other parts of the body (metastasize), making it harder to treat with surgery or other therapies.

list.title: Limited Treatment Options:
list.snippet: Currently, treatment options for pancreatic cancer are limited, and even with aggressive treatment, the five-year survival rate remains low.

text_blocks.snippet: While other cancers like lung and colorectal cancer have high mortality rates, their overall survival rates are higher than pancreatic cancer because they are sometimes diagnosed earlier and have more treatment options.
